_comment: Curated, real, geographically diverse flood/wetland-significant locations for VAMIKA's pre-seeded instant-demo cache (Tier 1). Coordinates are approximate region centers, not tied to any specific historical event date - the pre-seed script queries NASA CMR for whatever real NISAR acquisitions actually exist at each place and picks the best available real before/after pair. This list is version-controlled; backend/data/featured_cache.json (generated by the pre-seed script) holds the per-location analysis linkage and is NOT version-controlled. Trimmed to the 5 locations already successfully pre-seeded on the GCP VM - more can be added back once a future pre-seed batch run covers them (see git history for the full original 25-location list).

locations.name: Sundarbans
locations.blurb: The world's largest mangrove forest and a UNESCO World Heritage site, forming a critical natural flood buffer for the Ganges-Brahmaputra delta.

locations.name: Pantanal
locations.blurb: The world's largest tropical wetland, spanning Brazil, Bolivia and Paraguay, with an extreme seasonal flood pulse that drives one of the planet's richest concentrations of wildlife.

locations.name: Okavango Delta
locations.blurb: A UNESCO World Heritage inland river delta in the Kalahari Desert that floods seasonally, supporting an exceptional concentration of wildlife in an otherwise arid region.

locations.name: Amazon Floodplain (Iquitos)
locations.blurb: Seasonally-flooded Amazon varzea forest, where L-band SAR can see standing water beneath the forest canopy that optical satellites cannot.

locations.name: Po River Delta
locations.blurb: The Mediterranean's largest wetland and a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve, at the mouth of Italy's longest river.
